messages.author: 0dbfcf0efe4ff8fe
messages.subject: reporting of fitted (real) parameters with covariates
parts:
Hello,
The output for a fitted secr model (below) surprised me.  Here, "trav" is a categorical trap covariate with 4 levels. I called the level I wanted to be the reference level "A".
The reported real value of g0 "at base levels of covariates" does not equal exp(beta g0), rather, it  seems to be reporting the real value of g0 where trav = B (calculations at bottom).
The beta parameter names seem to indicate that secr.fit used trav = A as the reference ("base"?) level, so shouldn't the real value of g0 correspond to beta g0 where trav = A?
The first record in the traps object has trav = B.

I'm using secr version 2.9.5 with R (windows) version 3.2.1.
Thanks in advance,
Eric

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: reporting of fitted (real) parameters with covariates
parts:
Hi Eric

Yes, that is how predict.secr works. The base levels of covariates are those for the first observation in the dataset. When there are multiple covariates this is ensures that the prediction is done at a combination of levels that is in the data, rather than one that potentially lies outside.

It is definitely a trap for the unwary, and perhaps should be changed. Some tips that may help:
-- You can specify any levels you like in the 'newdata' argument of predict.secr, and this is the best route
--  If you are uncertain about the default levels, set the 'savenew' argument and inspect the resulting attribute (see code below)
-- To see how the default newdata is generated, try secr.make.newdata.

Murray

Example with ovenCH[[4]] in which the first individual is male (M) rather than female (F):

> fit <- secr.fit(ovenCH[[4]], CL = TRUE, model = g0~Sex, buffer = 250)

> pred <- predict(fit, savenew = TRUE)
> attr(pred, 'newdata')
  session Sex
1    2008   M

> pred
link    estimate SE.estimate          lcl         ucl
link    estimate SE.estimate         lcl       ucl
link    estimate SE.estimate          lcl         ucl
